thesis: The Qur'an forbids turning one's back in battle but allows only movements that still serve the fight, exposing every other retreat as fear breaking a communal trust.

flags.quote: The believers are forbidden from turning their backs when the lines meet, but the command is not simplistic bravado.
flags.issue: Major-sin passage presented as flatly general with zero acknowledgment of the ikhtilaf al-Tabari devotes most of his commentary to: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri/al-Hasan/Qatadah/al-Dahhak/Nafi' held 8:15-16 Badr-specific; 'Ata held it abrogated by the 8:66 takhfif (no obligation against more than twice one's number); Ibn Abbas + seven-destructive-sins hadith treat it general. No tadabbur-vs-fatwa line.

flags.quote: Anything else is not strategic humility. It is a surrender of trust.
flags.issue: Stated absolutely; as written it is STRICTER than any of the four editions' final positions (ignores the 8:66 two-to-one concession mainstream fiqh incorporates).

notes: Thesis grounded (two-exceptions reading carried by Ibn Kathir + Tabari; Tabari's tarjih matches the general framing). Fix surgical: Badr-specific-vs-general paragraph + 8:66 takhfif + tadabbur/fatwa line. Should not ship on a fleeing-from-battle passage without it.

thesis: Allah's help at Badr began by calming, cleansing, and inwardly fastening the believers before it unfolded into outward victory — real divine aid secures the heart before it secures the field.

flags.quote: That inward half is where the commentators part ways over the word *rijz*.
flags.issue: Claimed division not carried by the fetched editions — all four gloss rijz as the inward whispering; the only 'outward defilement' support is the English translator's parenthetical. Ikhtilaf exists in the wider tradition but is unverifiable in-pipeline.

flags.quote: Al-Tabari, commenting on the next verse, speaks of the blows falling by the hands of Allah's believing allies.
flags.issue: Off by one verse: the phrase occurs in Tabari on 8:14, not 8:13. Substance correct, location wrong.

flags.quote: Al-Muyassar glosses *kulla banan* as every extremity and joint - the fingers and limbs that hold and swing a weapon.
flags.issue: First half matches al-Muyassar exactly; the appositive is editorial rationale reading as part of his gloss.

notes: Strong, near-pass file flagged per the strict attributions-must-match rule, not substance. Check 4 handled WELL: 8:12's strike command kept in Badr context, addressee ikhtilaf acknowledged, file explicitly says commentators do not make it a standing instruction. All three flags are one-line fixes.
